_doc: The GM's per-run lead seed (direction v2 §5 — Rumors -> Leads). LeadSystem slots these at run start, deterministically per run-seed (a seeded RNG, never RNG-in-combat). A lead = {id, subject, where_hint, source, state, spawned_day}. 'map_pos' (P5) is the district map's PIN for this lead, in the canonical MAP-IMAGE space (map_v3.png px, world = px * MapProjection.CITY_SCALE) — authored at the lead's real site/door so the pin lands where following the hint takes you; a where_candidates lead carries map_pos PER CANDIDATE (the picked row supplies both hint and pin); omitted = no pin (the trail is a name, not a spot). 'source' is which NPC KNOWS the lead (source-gated reveal — an NPC only surfaces a lead whose source is them, OR whose subject matches a phrase in that NPC's knowledge[] in npcs.json; this keeps the who-knows-what in DATA, no NPC-id branch in engine logic). 'guaranteed' leads are always slotted (the §3 opener). 'where_candidates' is a weighted pool the GM picks a where_hint from per run (the reshuffle). 'respawn_where' seeds the fresh where_hint a COLD lead re-emerges at (perish -> the subject moved). 'prey_form' (M26 RETUNE #2 fix) names the hidden-Beyonder combat_form this lead points at (butcher_human/wren_human/mack_harbor); the Doom 'monsters left alive' driver counts a live hidden Beyonder ONLY once its lead has been SURFACED to the player (known) — an idle player is never taxed for prey they have not yet been told exists, but ignoring KNOWN prey costs Doom. Pure data linkage form<->lead, no NPC-id branch.

leads.subject: the butcher on Iron Cross Street, who hasn't been himself
respawn_where: the canal steps off Iron Cross

leads._note: M12 — the FIRST REAL HUNT made real (direction v2 §3/§6). Previously a where_candidates pool that pointed nowhere; now a REAL destination: subject = Sable Wren (the hidden Hunter-pathway Beyonder, npcs.json), where_hint = 'the Blackthorn corner' (her authored schedule/deed site, so following it ROUTES the player to the fight), pathway:hunter (so the advance is same-pathway). subject_key 'hunter' keeps the source-gate DATA-driven (constable_brom's beat knowledge names the corner). Downing her drops hunter_characteristic via Progression's PATHWAY-driven drop (M5), enabling the advance — the loop's payoff.
leads.subject: the butcher wasn't the only one — Sable Wren, the thief-taker on the Blackthorn corner, carries the same ruined blood

leads._note: M14 — the SECOND REAL HUNT (the Seq-8 player's meal, direction v2 §6). A lead pointing at leland_mack, the harbor poacher who lost control. Gated behind the first advance: after_advance:true means LeadSystem surfaces it ONLY AFTER Progression emits advanced (the post-advance hook wired in LeadSystem._ready). This preserves pacing: Wren is the Seq-9 meal; Mack is the Seq-8 meal, revealed by the city only once the player has proven they can handle the first hunt. where_hint = 'the harbor breakwater' (his authored schedule/deed site). pathway:hunter so the advance payoff keys off the same rule as all hunter foes. Source is constable_brom (his beat knowledge covers the harbor missing persons). subject_key 'hunter' keeps the source-gate DATA-driven.
leads.subject: the line-handler at the breakwater — Leland Mack — carries the same ruined blood; the docks missing persons are his kills

leads._note: M28 (direction v2 §6) — the HERMIT pathway's prey lead, mirroring the Hunter's hunter_prey_kell_kin. Points at old_neil, the alchemist who lost control to the Hidden Sage. subject = Old Neil, where_hint = his rooms (his authored schedule/deed site, so following it ROUTES the player to the fight), pathway:hermit (so the advance is same-pathway -> hermit_characteristic via the PATHWAY-driven drop). subject_key 'hermit' keeps the source-gate DATA-driven; source naya_brookes (a real Seer who senses a fellow occultist's wrongness). prey_form is DELIBERATELY omitted (empty): unlike the Hunter meals, ignoring the KNOWN-but-human Neil does not tax the Doom 'monsters left alive' driver — this keeps the shipped Hunter-run pacing (test_balance's 3 loose Beyonders) unperturbed; once Neil TRANSFORMS to neil_monster (monster:true) he is counted like any monster.
leads.subject: the alchemist Old Neil, who traded his grief to the Hidden Sage — the same starlight in his blood as any Hermit that lost the leash
leads.where_hint: Old Neil's rooms off the apothecary lane

leads._note: M30 (direction v2 §6) — the HERMIT pathway's SECOND prey lead (the Seq-8 meal), mirroring the Hunter's hunter_prey_mack_docks. Points at ledger_finch, the records clerk who stole and read a restricted forbidden volume and lost control. Gated behind the first advance (after_advance:true): LeadSystem surfaces it ONLY AFTER Progression emits advanced, exactly like the Hunter's Mack — Neil is the Seq-9 meal, Finch is the Seq-8 meal the city names only once the player has proven the first Hermit hunt. pathway:hermit so a same-pathway kill drops hermit_characteristic via the PATHWAY-driven drop (the ladder's second fuel), and so slot_run's pathway gate (M30 bug#3) keeps it out of Hunter runs. subject_key 'hermit' keeps the source-gate DATA-driven; source naya_brookes (the Seer who feels a second occultist's wrongness). where_hint is the university archive (her authored schedule/deed site, so following it ROUTES the player to the fight). prey_form is DELIBERATELY omitted (empty), like the neil lead: ignoring the KNOWN-but-human Finch does not tax the Doom 'monsters left alive' driver until she TRANSFORMS to finch_monster (monster:true) — keeping the shipped pacing unperturbed.
leads.subject: there is a second one — Ledger Finch at the university archive, ink to the elbows, carrying the same starlight-in-the-blood as any Hermit that read too deep and lost the leash
respawn_where: the archive reading room after dark

leads._note: M_death — the DEATH pathway's Seq-9 prey lead, mirroring hermit_prey_neil. Points at sister_auber; where_hint = her authored schedule/deed site (following it ROUTES the player to the fight). pathway:death -> same-pathway advance via the PATHWAY-driven drop, and slot_run's pathway gate keeps it out of Hunter/Hermit runs. source naya_brookes (the true Seer/medium senses the grave-cold on her). prey_form DELIBERATELY omitted (the hermit precedent — the human phase never taxes Doom; auber_monster counts once she transforms).
leads.subject: the lay-sister at Saint Selena's — Sister Auber — the plaza's dead answer her prayers, and the same grave-cold clings to her as to any Corpse Collector that lost the leash
leads.where_hint: the almshouse door at Saint Selena's
respawn_where: the paupers' rows behind the cathedral

leads._note: M_death — the DEATH pathway's SECOND prey lead (the Seq-8 meal), mirroring hermit_prey_finch/hunter_prey_mack_docks. after_advance:true — LeadSystem surfaces it ONLY AFTER Progression emits advanced (auber is the Seq-9 meal; the city names cassian once the first hunt is proven). pathway:death; source naya_brookes; prey_form DELIBERATELY omitted (same Doom-pacing reason).
leads.subject: there is a second one — Brother Cassian, the young curate — his miracles smell of the crypt, the same grave-cold in his blood, and the dead down there keep his hours
leads.where_hint: Saint Selena's crypt stair after dark
respawn_where: the cathedral nave after the last office

leads.subject: a cult courier moving something wrapped through the harbor after dark
chalk marks and candle-smoke found where the rite is being prepared
